title: The first versions: Austin Seven and Morris Mini-Minor
author: Caramagnols
excerpt: The Mini began under two BMC names, Austin Seven and Morris Mini-Minor, before the single Mini identity took over.
content:
At launch in 1959, the Mini did not begin as one simple marque name. BMC presented it as the Austin Seven and the Morris Mini-Minor, two almost identical versions sold through inherited Austin and Morris networks.

Two badges for one idea

The differences were mainly presentation details: grille, badges, trim and commercial habit. The engineering idea was the same. BMC used two names because the group still worked through two strong historic marques.

This double identity explains why period references can vary. A car may be called Austin Seven, Morris Mini-Minor or simply Mini depending on date, market and habit.

The Mini name wins

The public quickly retained the shorter name because it described the car better than the old marques did. The model became stronger than both launch badges.

The launch context is linked to why the Mini appeared in 1959. The later evolution continues in the Mini generations.
